Every one of the 14 amount cells was re-read from four high-dpi column strips at 1400 dpi, so the sum is not a full-page reading. That is +19.90 against the promoted Box D (13,113.81), and -0.10 against a '13,133.81' reading of the sheet's own over-written page subtotal. TRACE: the difference is NOT a missing or doubled row. (a) Every printed band was cropped: the grid is 15 data rows, rows 1-14 carry entries and row 15 rendered EMPTY, so no row was dropped; (b) no band is ~2x the 4.3% pitch, so ADDENDUM H3's two-entries-in-one-row trap is excluded; (c) the space below the last printed rule holds only the form's 'Subtotal for this page' label, so ADDENDUM F1.5 is excluded; (d) no row is voided, no banner line, no continuation line. What the page shows instead is a FILER COPY SLIP in exactly the digit he over-wrote: the schedule's subtotal has its hundreds digit corrected on top of itself, and the cover carries the UNCORRECTED hundreds digit (13,1_1_3.81 vs 13,1_3_3.81), which is precisely 20.00. The residual 0.10 between the rows (13,133.71) and a 13,133.81 subtotal is a filer addition slip that CANNOT be attributed uniquely — several cents cells (70.86 / 62.86 / 101.08 / 107.05 / 112.01) could each absorb it and every one of them reproduced cleanly at 1400 dpi — so per ADDENDUM C5 NOTHING WAS NUDGED and the rows stand verbatim.
